cases.title: Baseline API returns the requested Top-K rankings
cases.description:
Use cases: UC10/UC55 Generate Baseline Top-K Plays; UC18 Ranked List via API.

Related work: SCRUM-321.

Precondition: the backend has loaded its play-type data and the request uses a valid coach session.

  1. Send GET /rank-plays/baseline?season=2024-25&our=TOR&opp=BOS&k=5&w_off=0.7.

  2. Check the response metadata and each ranking.

Expected result: HTTP 200; season=2024-25, our_team=TOR, opp_team=BOS, k=5, w_off=0.7 and w_def=0.3 (allow normal floating-point rounding). The rankings array contains five items, each with PLAY_TYPE, PPP_PRED and PPP_GAP.

cases.title: Baseline API rejects missing or invalid parameters
cases.description:
Use cases: UC10/UC55 Generate Baseline Top-K Plays; UC18 Ranked List via API.

Related work: SCRUM-321.

Precondition: the backend has loaded its play-type data and the request uses a valid coach session.

  1. Start with GET /rank-plays/baseline?season=2024-25&our=TOR&opp=BOS&k=5&w_off=0.7.

  2. In separate requests, omit our; set k=-1; use season=invalid-season; then set our to an empty string. Keep the other parameters valid each time.

  3. Check the status and JSON error body.

Expected result: missing our and k=-1 return HTTP 422. The unknown season and empty our value return HTTP 400. Each response contains a detail field and no rankings result.

cases.title: Calibration trains on earlier seasons only
cases.description:

  2. Check that every training season is earlier than the test season and no held-out row is used for training.

  3. Check that raw PPP is excluded from FEATURE_COLS and that the report explains that some other inputs are same-season rates tied to the outcome.

  4. Change the held-out target values and feature scale, then check that the training-only inputs and fitted preprocessing settings stay unchanged.

Expected: Training and test rows stay separate and in time order. Scaling and reliability adjustments use only training data, and raw PPP is not an input. Changing the test data does not change fitted training settings, while the evaluation results respond as expected. The report explains that same-season inputs make this a historical evaluation; it does not prove future-game accuracy or rule out every outcome-related input. Using only earlier information and an untouched forecasting test set remains SCRUM-526.
